questions.q: How often will David praise Yahweh?
questions.a: David will praise Yahweh at all times.

questions.q: Who does David want to hear when he boasts in Yahweh?
questions.a: David wants the humble to hear it and rejoice.

questions.q: What is David asking people to do with him?
questions.a: David is asking them to magnify Yahweh and exalt his name together.

questions.q: What happened when David sought Yahweh?
questions.a: Yahweh answered David and delivered him from all his fears.

questions.q: What happens to those who look to Yahweh?
questions.a: They are radiant and their faces are not ashamed.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do when this afflicted man called out to him?
questions.a: Yahweh heard him and saved him from all his troubles.

questions.q: What does the angel of Yahweh do when he encamps around those who fear him?
questions.a: The angel of Yahweh rescues them.

questions.q: Who is the man who is happy?
questions.a: The man who takes refuge in Yahweh is happy.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say is true for those who fear Yahweh?
questions.a: There is no lack for those who fear Yahweh.

questions.q: What does David say about those who seek Yahweh?
questions.a: Those who seek Yahweh will not lack anything good.

questions.q: What does David invite the sons to do?
questions.a: David invites them to come and listen to him so that he can teach them the fear of Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say a man who desires life should do?
questions.a: He should guard his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit, turn away from evil, do good, seek peace, and pursue it.

questions.q: How does Yahweh pay attention to the righteous?
questions.a: Yahweh pays attention and listens when the righteous call to him for help.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the doers of evil?
questions.a: Yahweh will cut off their remembrance from the earth.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do when the righteous cry out?
questions.a: He hears and delivers them from all their troubles.

questions.q: To whom is Yahweh near?
questions.a: He is near the brokenhearted.

questions.q: Who does Yahweh save?
questions.a: Yahweh saves those with a crushed spirit.

questions.q: What happens to the righteous who have many troubles?
questions.a: Yahweh delivers him from all of them and guards all his bones.

questions.q: What will happen to the wicked?
questions.a: Evil will kill the wicked.

questions.q: What will happen to those who hate the righteous?
questions.a: Those who hate the righteous will be found guilty.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do for his servants?
questions.a: He redeems the soul of his servants, and those who take refuge in him will not be guilty.

commentary.text: David praises God, and encourages to trust him.

Verses 1–10 If we hope to spend eternity in praising God, it is fit that we should spend much of our time here in this work. He never said to any one, Seek ye me in vain. David's prayers helped to silence his fears; many besides him have looked unto the Lord by faith and prayer, and it has wonderfully revived and comforted them. When we look to the world, we are perplexed, and at a loss. But on looking to Christ depends our whole salvation, and all things needful thereunto do so also. This poor man, whom no man looked upon with any respect, or looked after with any concern, was yet welcome to the throne of grace; the Lord heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles. The holy angels minister to the saints, and stand for them against the powers of darkness. All the glory be to the Lord of the angels. By taste and sight we both make discoveries, and have enjoyment; Taste and see God's goodness; take notice of it, and take the comfort of it. He makes all truly blessed that trust in him. As to the things of the other world, they shall have grace sufficient for the support of spiritual life. And as to this life, they shall have what is necessary from the hand of God. Paul had all, and abounded, because he was content, Php 4:11–18. Those who trust to themselves, and think their own efforts sufficient for them, shall want; but they shall be fed who trust in the Lord. Those shall not want, who with quietness work, and mind their own business.

Let young persons set out in life with learning the fear of the Lord, if they desire true comfort here, and eternal happiness hereafter. Those will be most happy who begin the soonest to serve so good a Master. All aim to be happy. Surely this must look further than the present world; for man's life on earth consists but of few days, and those full of trouble. What man is he that would see the good of that where all bliss is perfect? Alas! few have this good in their thoughts. That religion promises best which creates watchfulness over the heart and over the tongue. It is not enough not to do hurt, we must study to be useful, and to live to some purpose; we must seek peace and pursue it; be willing to deny ourselves a great deal for peace’ sake. It is the constant practice of real believers, when in distress, to cry unto God, and it is their constant comfort that he hears them. The righteous are humbled for sin, and are low in their own eyes. Nothing is more needful to true godliness than a contrite heart, broken off from every self-confidence. In this soil every grace will flourish, and nothing can encourage such a one but the free, rich grace of the gospel of Jesus Christ. The righteous are taken under the special protection of the Lord, yet they have their share of crosses in this world, and there are those that hate them. Both from the mercy of Heaven, and the malice of hell, the afflictions of the righteous must be many. But whatever troubles befal them, shall not hurt their souls, for God keeps them from sinning in troubles. No man is desolate, but he whom God has forsaken.
